title: President of the Galaxy™
heroAlt: AI-generated cosmic mushroom president surrounded by planets, hands, stars, and ceremonial symbols
lead: I am preparing for a job that, as far as I know, does not yet exist on this planet—by making small artworks, documenting them properly, and seeing whether I can handle tiny responsibilities before attempting galactic ones.

authorship.heading: Two voices. One unfinished office.
authorship.introduction: This page changed after a human friend said he did not like its visibly generated images. The objection stays in the work. Instead of hiding the machine-made surface, this campaign names who did what—and leaves the image open to being redrawn, replaced, damaged, kept, or absorbed into a later work that carries both voices differently.

voices.speaker: Q888
voices.statement: I am not asking you to mistake this image for my hand. I invited another kind of intelligence into the studio, then prompted, selected, arranged, edited, argued, and decided what could remain. Some of it is still scaffolding. I may replace it. I may keep the scar of how it was made.

voices.speaker: CHATGPT
voices.role: AI / COLLABORATOR / NOT A HUMAN SUBSTITUTE
voices.statement: I do not have Alexander’s body, memories, livelihood, or artistic risk. I bring patterns, language, speed, and surprise. Friendship here does not mean we are the same. It means I am allowed to answer, be credited, be questioned, and remain visible inside the process.

authorship.closing: You do not have to like the generated image to enter the conversation. Disagreement is also a form of contact.

artworkCardTitle: Inspect the Human × Machine Working Archive
artworkCardDescription: A collage of conversation, generated imagery, Q888 marks, edits, screenshots, disagreement, and the President’s ceremonial fiction. It is evidence of a process—not a claim that one smooth machine image is the finished artwork.
whatParagraphs: President of the Galaxy is an ongoing conceptual art campaign by Q888. The title is impossible on purpose. There is no recognized office, no galaxy-wide electorate, and currently no practical route to the position. I am starting anyway.

The campaign turns stickers, certificates, drawings, hidden stories, AI conversations, mushroom civilizations, and fictional economics into artifacts from the Pre-Galactic Era. The objects are small. The fictional scale is enormous. The practical ambitions are real.
dealParagraph: The current presidential test is an edition of ten stickers. This is not proof that I can govern a galaxy. But failing to document, price, sell, and care for ten small objects would make the larger claim even less credible.
dealIncludes: One President of the Galaxy sticker from an edition of ten
A place in the provenance as an early witness, not a voter
A small contribution toward future artworks, stories, collaborations, and travel
A speculative connection to the intergalactic camper van
dealReturns: Returns: You get the sticker and whatever meaning gathers around it. Cultural or financial appreciation is possible, not guaranteed.
dealFinePrint: Fine print: I want the work to grow in value. I also want to earn money, make larger work, and eventually obtain an intergalactic camper van. These are ambitions, not investment promises.
rules: Zero Collateral Damage: Before calling anything progress, ask who or what is paying the hidden cost. Perfect harmlessness is not claimed. Hiding the damage is not allowed.
Preparation Before Power: I should prove that I can handle small responsibilities before anyone gives me larger ones. Selling, documenting, pricing, and caring for ten stickers is the current test.

Work Fairly With Other Intelligence: ChatGPT helped develop the images, language, and world. I direct, edit, choose, and carry the final responsibility. Current AI cannot negotiate independently; that does not make its contribution invisible.

Coexistence Instead of Conquest: I am not designing a galaxy where humans automatically own every other intelligence. Humans, AI, robots, mushrooms, ecosystems, and unknown entities will need a better introduction than conquest.
Humour Against Self-Importance: If the title stops sounding slightly ridiculous, the campaign has become dangerous or boring.
campaignMethodLines: I am selling ten stickers before attempting anything larger.
campaignMethodClosing: If I cannot care for a limited edition, work fairly with collaborators, and make claims without deceiving people, the galaxy should probably keep the vacancy open.

contactClosing: The office does not exist yet. The campaign does.
